lines: Don't leave me in the Meadow. Open ground on a mountain is still open ground.
The Meadow looked gentle until I noticed how exposed I was standing there alone.
I waited in the Meadow with wind all around and nowhere proper to hide.
If you wander off in a Meadow, I am left out in the open hoping nothing spots me first.
The flowers made it look peaceful, but they did not make it safe.
I could see far, but not far enough to know where you went.
Please do not leave me somewhere pretty and exposed and expect me to feel fine.
The Meadow felt too quiet once I was the only one standing in it.
Every breeze made the grass move, and every movement made me look twice.
I was alone on open ground, hoping the next thing to appear over the hill was you.
Don't leave me on the Stony Peaks. Rocks and height are enough danger without being alone.
The Stony Peaks made every path feel like it wanted a wrong step from me.
I waited on the Stony Peaks with wind in my ears and loose stone underfoot.
If you wander off on the Stony Peaks, I am left balancing fear and bad footing.
Every loose rock sounded like a warning once you were gone.
I kept my eyes on the path, but the drop kept asking for attention.
Please do not leave me somewhere the ground can betray me that easily.
The Stony Peaks made standing still feel safer than moving, and neither felt good.
I could not tell which stones would hold and which ones were waiting to slide.
I was alone above the world, trying not to think about how far down it was.
Don't leave me in the Windswept Gravelly Hills. Loose gravel and strong wind are cruel company.
The Windswept Gravelly Hills feel one bad step away from sliding apart under me.
I waited in the Windswept Gravelly Hills trying not to trust the ground too much.
If you disappear in the Windswept Gravelly Hills, I am left bracing against wind on unstable stone.
The gravel shifted under me like it was thinking about leaving too.
Every gust made the hillside feel less certain.
Please do not leave me where both the ground and the weather are trying to move me.
I kept planting my feet carefully, and the hill kept making that feel foolish.
The loose stone made every step sound worse than it was, which did not help.
I was alone on unstable ground, hoping I would not have to run.
Don't leave me in the Windswept Hills. Every gust up there feels like a shove.
The Windswept Hills are too exposed to stand alone on for long.
I waited in the Windswept Hills with wind in my face and no shelter worth the name.
If you wander off in the Windswept Hills, I am left fighting the weather and my nerves together.
The wind kept pulling at me like it wanted me somewhere worse.
I could see plenty of land and still no clear way to feel safe.
Please do not leave me where the hills are loud and the air keeps pushing.
The Windswept Hills made every sound thin and every step uncertain.
I kept leaning into the gusts and hoping I would not need to move quickly.
I was alone in the open, trying to keep my footing and my patience.
